title: BalancerPoolerV2.migrateMint is reachable while every available pause switch in the system is engaged, extending the pause-topology gap to the migration surface
description:
migrateMint has no `whenNotPaused` modifier (confirmed by the test test_migrateMint_runsWhenPaused which explicitly asserts the function executes after `pooler.pause()` flips the dispatcher's Pausable._paused). The function reaches into NFTMinterV2.burn and NFTMinterV2.mintFor — and per the prior audit (yield-claim-nft-06 RAW-002), neither burn nor mintFor honour NFTMinterV2's global `paused` flag either. Therefore migrateMint executes successfully when (a) BalancerPoolerV2.paused == true (Pausable on the dispatcher), AND (b) NFTMinterV2.paused == true (global Pauser-set flag). Both pause planes that an operator has at their disposal are bypassed.

During an incident, the operator-mental-model is 'engage every pause switch and investigate.' For migrateMint the operator must additionally: (i) call `NFTMinterV2.setAuthorizedBurner(pooler, false)` (one onlyOwner tx), AND (ii) call `NFTMinterV2.setAuthorizedMinter(pooler, false)` (one onlyOwner tx). Both are owner-controlled, not pauser-controlled, and require the owner key to be reachable. In a fast-moving incident (compromised pooler dispatcher contract, observed double-minting, anomalous id-4 supply, blocklist event upstream), the gap between 'pause' and 'authorized-burner / authorized-minter revocation' is the window in which migrateMint can keep issuing id-6 NFTs.

The surface this exposes is bounded: migrateMint is 1:1 (one id-4 burns to mint one id-6) and msg.sender is the burn target, so the function cannot create id-6 out of thin air — it consumes id-4 supply. The worst case during an incident is that id-4 holders continue to convert to id-6 while the rest of the protocol is supposed to be frozen. If the incident is *related to the id-4 cohort itself* (e.g., a flaw in the original dispatcher discovered after the migration opens, and id-4 supply is itself in dispute), the inability to freeze the migration via the pause role becomes operationally damaging.

This finding is a continuation of yield-claim-nft-06 RAW-001 (pool() pause-topology gap) and RAW-002 (mintFor ignores paused). The story-033 commit ADDS a third bypass to the same global-pauser surface, extending the documented gap to a new function.
exploit_path:
1. Global Pauser detects an incident (e.g., a flaw discovered in the original BalancerPoolerV2 lifecycle that means id-4 supply is contested, or a flaw in the new pooler discovered post-replaceDispatcher) and calls NFTMinterV2.pause(). The global `paused` flag is true. Operator believes mint and migration surfaces are frozen.
2. Operator also calls (or assumes some other path calls) BalancerPoolerV2.pause() via the setDispatcherActive(false) owner path. The dispatcher's Pausable._paused is true.
3. Despite both pause flags being engaged, any id-4 holder calls BalancerPoolerV2.migrateMint(amount, recipient). The call traverses migrateMint -> NFTMinterV2.burn -> NFTMinterV2.mintFor -> ERC1155 _mint. None of the four call sites consult either pause flag. Migration proceeds.
4. ClaimBurned and ClaimMintedFor events fire as if no incident. id-6 supply grows at the rate id-4 supply shrinks.
5. The operator-recovery action is to send two further owner-only txs: `NFTMinterV2.setAuthorizedBurner(pooler, false)` and `NFTMinterV2.setAuthorizedMinter(pooler, false)`. These txs require the owner key, which is the slowest control plane in the system. Until they land, migration continues.

The operationally damaging case is a *fast incident on id-4*: the protocol cannot stop id-4 holders from cashing out into id-6 quickly enough.
mainnet_realism_check: Pure on-chain control-flow. The test test_migrateMint_runsWhenPaused already confirms the bypass at the dispatcher level; the bypass at the NFTMinterV2 level is the existing yield-claim-nft-06 RAW-002 issue, still present at HEAD. No mock dependency.
recommendation: Either (a) add `whenNotPaused` to migrateMint (it composes with ATokenDispatcherV2's Pausable cleanly) and add `require(!INFTMinterV2(minter).paused(), "BalancerPoolerV2: minter paused")` so that both pause planes block migration; or (b) document explicitly that migrateMint is intentionally bypass-pause and that the operator's incident playbook MUST include the two setAuthorizedBurner / setAuthorizedMinter revocations alongside the standard pauses. Option (a) closes the gap; option (b) makes the gap legible to the operator. The status-quo of having a gap that the test suite asserts is intentional but no runbook documents is the worst of both worlds.
